findings.title: GSTR-3B net tax payable omits the reverse-charge liability (Table 3.1(d)) while still claiming its credit
findings.evidence: apps/api/domain/gst/gstr3b_computer.py:712-731 computes net_igst/cgst/sgst from `outward_taxable_*` only; `rcm_igst/cgst/sgst` (accumulated at lines 700-706) are never added to the liability. `itc_consumed_paise` (line 345-350) has the same omission. apps/api/services/gst_return_service.py:846 returns `net_tax_paise = result.net_igst + result.net_cgst + result.net_sgst`, which is what is stored on `gstr3b_returns.net_tax_paise` (routers/gst_workspace.py:578) and rendered as Table 6 "Total" (apps/web/app/gst/gstr3b/page.tsx:417-432). Verified by running compute_gstr3b with one intra-state sale (CGST 90000p + SGST 90000p) and one RCM inward supply (IGST 500p): rcm_igst=500, itc_avail_igst=500, net total = 179500p — i.e. the RCM credit REDUCED the tax payable by 500p and the matching 500p liability was never added. Nothing on either GST screen renders `working.rcm_inward` at all (grep for 'rcm' in apps/web/app/gst/gstr3b/page.tsx and apps/web/app/clients/[id]/compliance/gst/page.tsx returns nothing), although lib/data/gst.ts:93-97 types it.
findings.ca_experience: For any client with GTA freight, legal fees, director's remuneration, sponsorship, or rent from an unregistered landlord — i.e. most SMEs — the "Net Tax Payable" figure on the GSTR-3B screen is understated by twice the reverse-charge tax (the liability is not added, and its credit is deducted). The CA pays a challan for the wrong amount and the return short-pays. §49(4) does not permit the credit ledger to discharge 3.1(d) at all; it must be paid in cash. The filing-demo wizard says so in words (services/filing_demo/gstr3b.py:204-207, 330-332) but its Table 6.1 also builds `head_liability` from `taxable_{head}_paise` only (line 292), so it repeats the omission.
findings.market_standard: TallyPrime, Zoho Books and ClearTax all carry the 3.1(d) RCM liability into the Table 6.1 payment working as a cash-only row, and ClearTax flags an RCM self-invoice that has no matching cash payment.
findings.suggested_fix: Add `rcm_*` to the liability side of the Table 6 set-off as a CASH-ONLY head (never discharged from ITC), expose it in `working.net_payable` as a separate `cash_only_rcm_paise`, and render Table 3.1(d) and the cash total on both GSTR-3B screens. Add a unit test asserting that one RCM purchase with no sales yields net payable equal to the RCM tax, not zero.

findings.title: IGST on a zero-rated (export/SEZ with payment) supply is dropped from GSTR-3B Table 3.1(b)
findings.evidence: apps/api/domain/gst/gstr3b_computer.py:665-667 — for `supply_type == "zero_rated"` only `outward_zero_rated += sign * taxable_amount_paise` is accumulated; igst_paise/cgst/sgst/cess are ignored. apps/api/domain/gst/gstr3b_computer.py:415-418 hardcodes `"osup_zero": {..., "iamt": 0, "camt": 0, "samt": 0, "csamt": 0}`. Verified: a zero-rated sale of 10_000_00p carrying 1_800_00p IGST produces outward_zero_rated=1000000, outward_taxable_igst=0, and payload osup_zero = {'txval': 10000, 'iamt': 0, ...}.
findings.ca_experience: An exporter who exports WITH payment of IGST (the route taken to get the automatic §16(3)(b) refund) files a GSTR-3B declaring the export turnover but zero IGST. Output tax is understated by the entire export IGST, the return does not reconcile with GSTR-1 Table 6A, and the ICEGATE refund has no declared liability behind it. The books-vs-ledger reconciliation in gst_return_service will also flag a permanent mismatch because the GL carries the credit to the output account.
findings.market_standard: Every GST product separates 3.1(b) into taxable value AND IGST, because export-with-payment is one of the two statutory routes under §16(3).
findings.suggested_fix: Accumulate igst/cess on `zero_rated` supplies into a dedicated `outward_zero_rated_igst`/`_cess` pair and emit them in `osup_zero`. Pin with a test using an export-with-payment invoice.

findings.title: The 2A/2B reconciliation screen tells the CA on-screen that ITC is capped at 105% — superseded law since 01-01-2022
findings.evidence: apps/web/app/gst/reconciliation/page.tsx:628 renders a blue info banner reading "CGST Rule 36(4): ITC is restricted to 105% of eligible credit appearing in GSTR-2A/2B"; repeated at line 894 ("ITC subject to 105% cap of GSTR-2A eligible credit") and in the file docstrings at lines 7 and 217, and in apps/web/app/gst/gstr3b/page.tsx:7. The backend is correct and explicitly contradicts it: apps/api/domain/gst/gstr3b_computer.py:5-7 and 545-551 cite Notification 40/2021-Central Tax (w.e.f. 1 Jan 2022) removing the 105% provisional buffer, with `_RULE_36_4_NUMERATOR = 100`.
findings.ca_experience: A CA reading the reconciliation screen is told they may claim 5% more ITC than the invoices matched in GSTR-2B support. Acting on it over-claims credit that has to be reversed with interest under §50 and attracts a §73/§74 notice. The two halves of the product state different law about the same rule.
findings.market_standard: ClearTax, IRIS and Cygnet all removed the 105%/110%/120% language when Rule 36(4) was substituted and §16(2)(aa) came in; their recon screens now show strict invoice-level 2B matching.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace all five occurrences with the current rule: §16(2)(aa) with Rule 36(4) as substituted by Notification 40/2021-CT — credit only on invoices communicated in GSTR-2B, no percentage buffer. Add a lint/test that greps the web tree for "105%" near "36(4)".

findings.title: GSTR-2B reconciliation never reads the books, does not parse a real GSTR-2B JSON, and persists nothing
findings.evidence: apps/api/routers/gst_workspace.py:824-834 — `book_invoices = raw.get("book_invoices", [])`, i.e. the BOOKS side is supplied by the caller inside the pasted JSON; `b2b_invoices = raw.get("data", {}).get("docDetails", []) or raw.get("invoices", [])` keyed on `inv.get("sgstin")`. A genuine GSTR-2B download is `data.docdata.b2b[] = {ctin, inv:[{inum, dt, val, ...}]}` — neither `docDetails` nor `sgstin` appears in it. The UI is a bare textarea: apps/web/app/clients/[id]/compliance/gst/page.tsx:1233 placeholder "Paste GSTR-2B JSON here (include book_invoices array for reconciliation)". Nothing anywhere INSERTs into `gstr2a_records` — grep across apps/api and apps/web finds only reads (services/gst_return_service.py:383, apps/web/lib/data/gst.ts:265), so `_gstr2a_for_period` always returns [] and `_apply_rule_36_4_cap` always takes its no-data branch. The separate /gst/reconciliation screen persists nothing either (no supabase call in the whole file).
findings.ca_experience: A CA pastes the GSTR-2B JSON downloaded from the portal and gets "Matched 0, Mismatched 0, Missing 0" — a clean result that means nothing, because no book invoice was ever compared. The alternative screen (/gst/reconciliation) requires exporting the purchase register out of PracticeSync and re-uploading it as CSV, and its result vanishes on refresh. The single most-performed monthly task in an Indian practice — ITC 2B matching — cannot actually be done here, and the Rule 36(4) working printed on the return says "gstr2a_record_count: 0" for every client for ever.
findings.market_standard: ClearTax, IRIS Sapphire, Cygnet and Zoho Books ingest the portal 2B JSON/Excel directly, match against the purchase register already in the product, persist the match state per invoice, support fuzzy matching on invoice number, carry unmatched items forward month to month, and produce a supplier follow-up list.
findings.suggested_fix: Parse the real GSTR-2B envelope (`data.docdata.b2b/b2ba/cdnr/cdnra/impg`), persist each row to `gstr2a_records` with its `itcavl`/`rsn` flags, read the books side server-side from `purchase_bills`, persist per-invoice match state, and expose an exact→fuzzy→manual matching workflow. Then Rule 36(4)/§16(2)(aa) can be applied invoice-wise rather than as an aggregate cap.

findings.title: CGST/SGST credit is never cross-utilised against IGST liability, so cash payable is overstated
findings.evidence: apps/api/domain/gst/gstr3b_computer.py:714-728 — the set-off applies IGST credit to IGST liability and splits any excess over CGST/SGST, but CGST credit is only ever set off against CGST (`net_cgst = max(0, outward_taxable_cgst - avail_cgst)`) and SGST only against SGST. §49(5)(b) and (c) require the balance of CGST credit and of SGST credit to be applied next against IGST. Verified: IGST liability 1_80_000p with CGST credit 1_00_000p and SGST credit 1_00_000p returns net_igst=180000, net_cgst=0, net_sgst=0 — the correct answer is nil payable. No test covers this direction (tests/test_gst_engine.py:319-330 covers only the IGST-excess case).
findings.ca_experience: Any client who buys intra-state and sells inter-state — a Maharashtra trader shipping to other states, an e-commerce seller, a service provider with out-of-state customers — is told to pay IGST in cash while their CGST and SGST credit sits unused. On the run above the CA is asked for ₹1,800 cash when ₹0 is due. The "Carried forward" tile on the screen (apps/web/app/gst/gstr3b/page.tsx:438-451) then also reports the stranded credit as carried forward, so both halves of the screen are wrong together.
findings.market_standard: TallyPrime and ClearTax implement §49(5) with §49A/49B and Rule 88A in full, and offer the taxpayer the same set-off preference the portal offers on the 6.1 screen.
findings.suggested_fix: Implement the full §49(5) ladder: IGST credit → IGST, then CGST/SGST in any proportion (Rule 88A); CGST credit → CGST, then IGST; SGST credit → SGST, then IGST; never CGST↔SGST (§49(5)(e)/(f)). Pin with tests for each of the four directions.

findings.title: Non-GST outward supplies are dropped from GSTR-3B Table 3.1(e) and counted nowhere
findings.evidence: apps/api/domain/gst/gstr3b_computer.py:663-671 — the supply-type branch handles `nil_rated`/`exempt`, `zero_rated` and `taxable`; `non_gst` matches none of them and falls through with no accumulator. Line 424 hardcodes `"osup_nongst": {"txval": 0}`. Verified: a 50_000_00p non_gst sale gives outward_nil_exempt=0 and osup_nongst {'txval': 0}. The GSTR-1 builder does handle it correctly (domain/gst/gstr1_builder.py:379-383 routes `non_gst` to `ngsup_amt` in Table 8), so the two returns disagree on the same invoice.
findings.ca_experience: A client dealing in petrol, diesel, alcohol for human consumption or electricity — petrol pumps, liquor retailers, and any business with an ancillary non-GST line — files a GSTR-3B that omits that turnover entirely, while their GSTR-1 Table 8 declares it. The GSTR-1 vs 3B turnover comparison on the portal flags the difference and the annual return will not tie.
findings.market_standard: Tally and Zoho both carry non-GST supplies to 3.1(e) and to GSTR-1 Table 8, and reconcile the two.
findings.suggested_fix: Add an `outward_non_gst` accumulator for `supply_type == "non_gst"` and emit it in `osup_nongst.txval`. Add a parity test asserting GSTR-1 Table 8 `ngsup_amt` equals GSTR-3B 3.1(e) for the same period.

findings.title: Deemed exports and SEZ supplies are filed as physical exports in Table 6A, losing the recipient's GSTIN; and an export with payment of IGST is filed as WOPAY
findings.evidence: apps/api/domain/gst/classifier.py:100-115 — `invoice_type in ("SEZ_with_payment","SEZ_without_payment","Deemed_export")` all route to EXP_WP/EXP_WOP, and the fallback comment says "assume no IGST payment (LUT)". `TransactionForClassification` carries no igst field, so payment-of-IGST cannot be detected. apps/api/domain/gst/gstr1_builder.py:527-553 `_build_exp` emits rows with `exp_typ` WPAY/WOPAY and `sbpcode`/`sbnum`/`sbdt` empty, and no `ctin`. Verified: a Deemed_export invoice to GSTIN 27AAAAA0000A1Z5 carrying 1_800_00p IGST produced `exp: [{exp_typ: "WOPAY", inv:[{inum:"INV1", ... }]}]` with the recipient GSTIN absent; and a zero_rated invoice carrying IGST classified as EXP_WOP. `_build_b2b` (line 219) would emit the raw literal `"SEZ_with_payment"` as `inv_typ` if such an invoice ever reached it, where GSTN's enum is R/SEWP/SEWOP/DE.
findings.ca_experience: An SEZ supplier's or a deemed exporter's customer never sees the supply in their GSTR-2B, so they lose the credit and the §54 deemed-export refund has nothing to match against. A real exporter who paid IGST is declared WOPAY, so the ICEGATE/GSTN cross-check that triggers the automatic IGST refund never fires and the refund simply does not arrive. Shipping bill number and date — mandatory for the 6A refund match — are always blank.
findings.market_standard: TallyPrime and ClearTax keep SEZ (6B) and deemed export (6C) in the b2b section with inv_typ SEWP/SEWOP/DE and the recipient GSTIN, keep 6A for exports only, decide WPAY vs WOPAY from whether IGST was charged, and require shipping bill details on 6A rows.
findings.suggested_fix: Split the export category: EXP_WP/EXP_WOP for `place_of_supply == "96"` only (WPAY when igst_paise > 0), and route SEZ_with_payment/SEZ_without_payment/Deemed_export into the b2b section with inv_typ SEWP/SEWOP/DE. Add shipping-bill columns to the sales invoice and require them on 6A rows.

findings.title: GSTR-1 Table 7 (B2CS) uses a blended rate inferred from the whole invoice, producing rates that do not exist
findings.evidence: apps/api/domain/gst/gstr1_builder.py:296-338 `_build_b2cs` calls `_infer_rate(inv)` (line 273-279: total tax × 10000 // taxable value) and keys the grouping on that single rate — it never reads `inv.lines`, unlike `_build_invoice_items` which correctly groups by line rate. Verified: a B2C invoice with a 5% line (1_000_00p) and an 18% line (1_000_00p) produced a single row `{'sply_ty':'INTRA','rt': 11.5, 'txval': 2000.0, 'camt': 115.0, 'samt': 115.0}`.
findings.ca_experience: Any multi-rate B2C business — a kirana store, a pharmacy, a restaurant selling both 5% and 18% items, a hardware shop — has nearly every counter sale filed under an invented rate. GSTN validates `rt` against the notified rate list and rejects the upload, so the CA gets an opaque portal error on a return they cannot fix from inside the product; and even where it uploads, the rate-wise B2C turnover the department reads is wrong.
findings.market_standard: Every product splits Table 7 one row per (rate, place of supply, supply type), taken from the invoice lines.
findings.suggested_fix: Rewrite `_build_b2cs` to iterate `inv.lines` and key on (line rate, place of supply, is_interstate), falling back to `_infer_rate` only for a header-only invoice with no lines. Add a test with a two-rate B2C invoice.

findings.title: The correction window always reports 30 November — the "or the annual return, whichever is earlier" limb is never wired
findings.evidence: apps/api/services/gst_amendment_service.py:69-73 accepts `annual_return_filed_on: Optional[date] = None` and passes it to `window_for` at line 101-102, but no caller ever supplies it: routers/gst_workspace.py:1105-1106 calls `outstanding_amendments(get_supabase(), current_user["firm_id"], client_id, period)` and routers/gst.py:471 the same. A grep for `annual_return_filed_on` across apps/api (excluding tests) returns only the four definition/pass-through sites. `domain/gst/correction_window.py:240-261` therefore always computes `closes == november_30_cutoff` and `shortened_by_annual_return == False`.
findings.ca_experience: A client who filed GSTR-9 for FY 2025-26 in August 2026 lost the ability to amend that year in August. PracticeSync tells the CA the window is open until 30 November 2026 and lists the amendment as actionable. The CA prepares an amendment that the portal will refuse, and — worse — believes an unclaimed ITC item is still available under §16(4) when it is not. CLAUDE.md names this exact failure mode as the reason `correction_window_closes()` exists.
findings.market_standard: ClearTax and IRIS both key the amendment deadline off the earlier of 30 November and the actual GSTR-9 filing date recorded for the client.
findings.suggested_fix: Resolve the GSTR-9 filing date server-side (gstr1_returns where return_type='gstr9' and status='submitted', or the `filings` row) and pass it into `outstanding_amendments`. Add a test where an August GSTR-9 closes an amendment the November cutoff would have left open.

findings.title: GSTR-9 is a tab that can never hold anything: no computation, and no UI that creates a draft
findings.evidence: apps/api/services/gst_return_service.py:1156-1163 states plainly "There is no gstr9 computation builder in domain/gst yet"; `gstr9_summary_from_returns` (line 1180-1256) only counts which months have a filed GSTR-1/3B and sums the filed GSTR-1 headers — no Tables 4-19. `POST /api/gst-workspace/gstr9` exists (routers/gst_workspace.py:944) but a grep of apps/web for `gst-workspace/gstr9` finds only the GET at apps/web/app/clients/[id]/compliance/gst/page.tsx:1386. The tab's empty state (line 1435-1438) says "Drafts are saved from the year's reviewed GSTR-1 and GSTR-3B returns" — nothing does that. The "File (demo)" button (line 1465) only renders when a draft exists, so it is unreachable.
findings.ca_experience: A CA opens GST → GSTR-9 for any client and any year and sees "No GSTR-9 draft for FY 2025-26 yet" for ever, with no button to create one. GSTR-9 is the single highest-fee annual GST engagement in a practice, and the product advertises it in navigation and cannot produce a single number of it — no Table 4 outward, no Table 6 ITC bifurcation (inputs/capital goods/input services), no Table 8 2A reconciliation, no Table 9 tax paid, no Tables 10-13 for the next-year adjustments, no Table 17/18 HSN.
findings.market_standard: ClearTax, IRIS and Winman all auto-populate GSTR-9 from the year's filed GSTR-1/3B plus GSTR-2A, show the Table 8 differences, and produce the GSTR-9 JSON. GSTR-9C (reconciliation statement, §44(2)) is absent here too.
findings.suggested_fix: Build `domain/gst/gstr9_builder.py` deriving Tables 4-8 and 17 from the year's filed returns plus the books, with the Table 6 ITC bifurcation as an explicit CA input where the books cannot supply it. Add a "Compute from filed returns" button on the GSTR-9 tab that calls the existing save endpoint. Until then, hide the tab rather than showing a dead one.

findings.title: QRMP quarterly returns cannot be computed, saved or recorded — every period in the return engine is one calendar month
findings.evidence: apps/api/services/gst_return_service.py:67-77 `_period_bounds("MMYYYY")` returns the first and last day of ONE calendar month, and `gstr1_from_books` / `gstr3b_from_books` are built on it. apps/api/services/gst_filing_record_service.py:60-75 duplicates the same monthly bounds, so a filed quarterly return locks one month, not three. Every UI period input is monthly: apps/web/app/gst/gstr3b/page.tsx:51-63 builds YYYY-MM options; the client workspace takes a raw MMYYYY string. By contrast the DUE DATES are fully QRMP-aware (apps/api/services/compliance_engine.py:118-162, routers/gst_workspace.py:68-95 `_gst_regime`) and the dashboard shows PMT-06 and IFF dates.
findings.ca_experience: A quarterly filer — anyone with preceding-year turnover up to ₹5 crore, i.e. the SME segment this product targets — is shown the correct 13th/22nd/24th due dates and then cannot produce the return they are due. The CA has to compute three separate monthly GSTR-3Bs and add them by hand, and the period lock only covers the last month of the quarter. IFF (Rule 59(2), B2B only, first two months) has no builder at all, so the QRMP client's customers wait a quarter for their credit.
findings.market_standard: ClearTax, Zoho Books and TallyPrime all support quarterly GSTR-1/3B periods and generate IFF for months 1 and 2.
findings.suggested_fix: Make the period a (start, end) range derived from the client's `gst_filing_frequency` rather than a MMYYYY month, thread it through both from-books builders, the filing record and the screens, and add an IFF builder that emits b2b/b2ba/cdnr/cdnur only.

findings.title: The "Add GST Filing" modal on /gst throws on every save — the period is "MMM YYYY" and is parsed with split("-")
findings.evidence: apps/web/app/gst/page.tsx:65-72 `buildMonthOptions()` builds options whose `value` is the label, e.g. "May 2026". apps/web/app/gst/page.tsx:186-188 in `handleSave`: `const [pYear, pMonth] = period.split("-").map(Number); const periodStart = ...; const periodEnd = new Date(pYear, pMonth, 0).toISOString().slice(0, 10);`. Verified in node: pYear=NaN, pMonth=undefined, periodStart="NaN-undefined-01", and `new Date(NaN, NaN, 0).toISOString()` throws RangeError "Invalid time value", which the surrounding try/catch turns into the modal error text.
findings.ca_experience: Every attempt to add a GST filing row from the main GST tracker fails with "Invalid time value". The tracker can only ever show rows seeded elsewhere; the CA cannot add one manually.
findings.market_standard: Not applicable — this is a straightforward defect in a primary create path.
findings.suggested_fix: Make MONTH_OPTIONS carry a machine value (`YYYY-MM`) separate from the display label, and have `getDueDate` and `handleSave` both read the machine value. Add a component test that saves a filing.

findings.title: The module's most differentiating backend work — amendments, exception report, ITC register, advances, portal sync — has no screen at all
findings.evidence: A grep of apps/web for each endpoint returns nothing: `gst-workspace/gstr1/amendments` (routers/gst_workspace.py:1082), `gst-workspace/gstr1/exceptions` (line 1120), `gst/gstr1/with-amendments` (routers/gst.py:434), `gst-workspace/itc/register` + `/reversal` + `/reclaim` (lines 1187, 1204, 1231), `gst-workspace/gstr1/advances` (line 1252), `POST gst-workspace/gstr9` (line 944), and the whole `/api/gst-portal` router (165 lines). The only one wired is `itc/rule37` (apps/web/lib/data/gst.ts:382). apps/api/routers/gst.py:437-445 says so itself about the amendment path: "NOTHING CONNECTED THE TWO: there was no route that produced the merged payload" — the route now exists and still has no caller.
findings.ca_experience: The CA cannot see what corrections an earlier filed period needs, cannot see how the books have drifted from a filed GSTR-1, cannot classify a posted reversal journal as a Rule 37 reversal (so 4(B)(2) is always nil unless someone POSTs the API by hand), and cannot see unadjusted advances. These are precisely the features that would differentiate the product; they are built, tested and invisible.
findings.market_standard: ClearTax and IRIS surface an amendment worklist and a books-vs-filed exception report as first-class screens; the ITC reversal/reclaim register is a standard ledger in IRIS and Cygnet.
findings.suggested_fix: Add tabs to the client GST workspace for Amendments (with a "Compute with amendments" action that calls /gstr1/with-amendments), Exceptions, ITC Register and Advances. The API shapes are stable and tested; this is UI work.

findings.title: Two contradictory "filed" states: /gst marks filings in compliance_calendar over PostgREST and never writes the filings row the period lock reads
findings.evidence: apps/web/app/gst/page.tsx:643-652 (`handleMarkFiled`) and 379-388 (bulk) write `filing_status`, `filed_date`, `arn_number` straight to `compliance_calendar` via `getSupabaseClient()` — no API call, so `rbac()` never runs and `record_filing` is never invoked. The genuine path is routers/gst_workspace.py:523-541 / 728-746, which calls `record_filing` into `filings` — the only table `journal_period_lock_reason` (migrations/266_editable_journals_until_locked_or_filed.sql:290) reads. apps/api/services/gst_filing_record_service.py:12-21 documents that an empty `filings` table makes the lock unreachable.
findings.ca_experience: A CA who marks GSTR-3B filed from the main GST tracker sees it green there, sees it still "draft" in the client GST workspace, and gets NO period lock — journals inside a filed period stay editable, so the books can move under a return already with the government. Two screens disagree about whether the same return is filed.
findings.market_standard: Tally's Edit Log and ClearTax both freeze a period once a return is marked filed, from whichever screen records it.
findings.suggested_fix: Route the tracker's mark-filed through `PATCH /api/gst-workspace/{gstr1,gstr3b}/{id}/status` so `record_filing` runs, or have the tracker read filing state from the returns tables rather than maintaining a second one in `compliance_calendar`.

findings.title: GSTR-1 Table 11 advance tax is computed into the filed payload while the advances report tells the CA it is not computed — and GSTR-3B never carries the same liability
findings.evidence: apps/api/services/gst_advance_service.py:126-182 `table_11_sections` DOES compute `at`/`txpd` rows with CGST/SGST/IGST split (via `split_inclusive_charge`) whenever `clients.gst_advance_tax_applicable` is true and the receipt carries `gst_rate_bps` and `place_of_supply`; services/gst_return_service.py:1093-1099 merges them into the filed payload. The same module's `advances_report` (line 235-244) returns `"table_11_computed": False` with "PracticeSync does not compute GSTR-1 Table 11", the module docstring (lines 27-32) says "Nothing has ever been declared in 11A", and routers/gst_workspace.py:1245-1249 repeats "This reports; it computes no tax". Separately, `compute_gstr3b` has no advance input at all — grep for "advance" in domain/gst/gstr3b_computer.py returns nothing.
findings.ca_experience: For a services client with advance tax switched on, tax on advances is silently added to the GSTR-1 the CA files, while the screen that exists to review advances says the product computes none — so nobody checks the figure. And GSTR-3B, which is where that tax is actually PAID under 3.1(a), never includes it: GSTR-1 declares a liability the 3B does not, the portal's GSTR-1 vs 3B comparison flags it, and the tax is never remitted.
findings.market_standard: Zoho Books and ClearTax carry advance receipts into GSTR-1 Table 11A and into GSTR-3B 3.1(a) together, and reverse them in 11B when the invoice is raised.
findings.suggested_fix: Either wire advances into GSTR-3B 3.1(a) and correct the report text and the docstring, or stop merging `at`/`txpd` into the payload. The two must agree; today they contradict each other in the same request.

findings.title: The GSTR-1 validator never runs on the path a CA actually uses
findings.evidence: apps/api/domain/gst/validator.py:186-202 `validate_gstr1` (duplicate invoice numbers, invalid place of supply, CGST≠SGST intra-state, IGST on an intra-state supply, tax arithmetic, out-of-period invoice dates) is invoked only from `POST /api/gst/gstr1/build` (routers/gst.py:520) and `POST /api/gst/validate/gstr1` (line 557). `gstr1_from_books` (services/gst_return_service.py:963-1136) never calls it, and neither does `/gstr1/with-amendments`; the only validation on the from-books path is `_validator.validate_gstin(gstin) + validate_period(period)` on the FILER's own GSTIN (routers/gst.py:423). Neither /gst/gstr1 nor the client GST workspace calls `/gstr1/build` — apps/web/lib/data/gst.ts:500 posts to `/api/gst/gstr1/from-books`.
findings.ca_experience: "Compute from Books" returns a GSTR-1 with no validation at all. A customer with a malformed GSTIN, a duplicate invoice number, a missing place of supply, or CGST≠SGST on an intra-state invoice goes straight into the payload; the CA discovers it as an opaque rejection from the offline tool or the portal, with no line number. The GSTR-1 screen has a "Validation warnings" area that is always empty on this path.
findings.market_standard: ClearTax and IRIS run 40-60 pre-filing validations on the prepared return and list the offending invoices before the JSON is produced.
findings.suggested_fix: Call `validate_gstr1` inside `gstr1_from_books` over the invoices it built and return the errors/warnings alongside the payload, and render them on both GSTR-1 screens. Use `domain/gst/gstin.py`'s check-digit validator for counterparty GSTINs rather than the shape regex.

findings.title: The HSN digit requirement is computed and then never applied or warned about, and the thresholds are the pre-2021 ones
findings.evidence: apps/api/domain/gst/gstr1_builder.py:558-568 sets 6 digits above ₹5 crore, 4 above ₹1.5 crore, 0 below. Notification 78/2020-Central Tax (15-10-2020, w.e.f. 01-04-2021) replaced that with: AATO above ₹5 crore → 6 digits on all invoices; AATO up to ₹5 crore → 4 digits on B2B (B2C optional). There is no ₹1.5 crore tier any more. Worse, the truncation is a no-op: line 587 `code = (line.hsn_sac_code or "")[:max(required_digits, len(line.hsn_sac_code or ""))]` — the slice length is never less than the code length. Verified: at ₹10 crore turnover a 2-digit HSN "99" is emitted unchanged as `hsn_sc: "99"` and an 8-digit code is emitted at 8.
findings.ca_experience: A ₹10-crore client whose masters carry 4-digit codes files a Table 12 the portal rejects, with nothing in the product having warned them. A ₹2-crore client is told 4 digits are required on the wrong statutory basis. Nothing checks that a code is a valid HSN at all.
findings.market_standard: Tally and ClearTax validate HSN length against AATO before the return is generated and list every invoice line that fails; GSTN's own Table 12 Phase-3 validation (from the Jan-2025 return period) rejects free-text HSN and splits Table 12 into separate B2B and B2C tabs — this builder emits one flat list.
findings.suggested_fix: Update the thresholds to Notification 78/2020, turn `_required_hsn_digits` into a VALIDATION (report every line whose code is shorter than required) rather than an unused truncation, and split Table 12 into B2B and B2C.

findings.title: GSTR-1 Table 13 (documents issued) is missing the serial-number range the form requires
findings.evidence: apps/api/domain/gst/gstr1_builder.py:698-702 emits `"docs": [{"num": count, "cancel": 0, "net_issue": count}]` — `num` is set to the COUNT of documents, and there is no `from`, `to` or `totnum`. Table 13 of FORM GSTR-1 asks for Sr. No. From, Sr. No. To, Total Number and Cancelled per nature of document, and `num` in the GSTN docs array is the row index, not a count. `cancel` is hardcoded 0 even though the builder can see cancelled documents. tests/test_gstr1_payload_matches_gstn_utility.py:115-160 asserts only `doc_num` and `doc_typ`, never the docs array's shape.
findings.ca_experience: The documents-issued table uploads (if at all) with no invoice serial range and zero cancellations, so the department's continuity check on invoice numbering has nothing to read, and a cancelled invoice series is never disclosed. Table 13 became a mandatory table from the January 2025 return period.
findings.market_standard: Tally and ClearTax derive the From/To serial range and the cancelled count directly from the document numbering series.
findings.suggested_fix: Emit `{num: <row index>, from: <first serial>, to: <last serial>, totnum: <count>, cancel: <cancelled count>, net_issue: totnum - cancel}` per nature, taken from the document series. Verify the key names against the current GSTN offline tool before shipping.

findings.title: Rule 36(4) is applied as an aggregate per-head cap, not invoice-level 2B matching, and the capped book figure includes credit that is not in 2B
findings.evidence: apps/api/domain/gst/gstr3b_computer.py:554-565 `_apply_rule_36_4_cap` compares the SUM of book ITC per head against the SUM of the 2A records per head and truncates. Rule 36(4) as substituted by Notification 40/2021-CT with §16(2)(aa) is an invoice-level test — credit is available only on invoices communicated in GSTR-2B — not an aggregate percentage. Further, `book_igst` (line 660) is the sum over ALL purchases including reverse-charge self-assessed tax (which does not appear in 2B's b2b section) and any import IGST, so the cap can trim genuine credit; and when the cap fires, nothing says WHICH invoices were disallowed.
findings.ca_experience: If 2B data ever were loaded, a client with RCM or import credit would see their ITC silently trimmed to the 2B b2b total, with a single boolean `cap_applied` and no invoice list. Today the cap can never fire at all because nothing writes `gstr2a_records` (see GST-04), so the working always shows "gstr2a_record_count: 0".
findings.market_standard: ClearTax, IRIS and Cygnet compute eligible ITC invoice by invoice against 2B, keep RCM and import IGST outside the matching set, and show the disallowed invoices.
findings.suggested_fix: After GST-04 lands, replace the aggregate cap with per-invoice eligibility (matched in 2B, `itcavl == 'Y'`), exclude RCM and IMPG from the matched set, and report the unmatched invoices as the reason for the difference.

findings.title: One GSTIN per client — no multi-state / multi-branch registration model
findings.evidence: apps/api/migrations/001_initial_schema.sql:28 defines `clients.gstin TEXT CHECK (...)` — a single column; there is no `client_gstins` / registrations table anywhere in migrations. `_client_gstin` (routers/gst.py:344-350) reads that one value, and every return is keyed on `(client_id, period)` (UNIQUE, migration 036), so a second GSTIN for the same client cannot have its own GSTR-1 or GSTR-3B row.
findings.ca_experience: Any client registered in more than one state — a manufacturer with a depot, a services firm with two offices, an e-commerce seller holding registrations for warehouse states — cannot be handled. The CA has to create a fake second "client" per GSTIN, which then breaks the accounting side (one entity, two ledgers) and every client-scoped report.
findings.market_standard: TallyPrime supports multi-GSTIN per company; Zoho Books supports GST branches; ClearTax and IRIS model a client as a PAN with many GSTINs and give a PAN-level dashboard across them.
findings.suggested_fix: Introduce a `client_gst_registrations` table (client_id, gstin, state_code, filing_frequency, registration_type, effective dates), key the returns tables on registration_id rather than client_id, and add a GSTIN selector to every GST screen. This is the largest structural change in the module and should be sequenced before more return-level work.

findings.title: No §50 interest and no §47 late fee anywhere in the product
findings.evidence: A grep for late fee / §47 / §50 across apps/api/domain and apps/api/services finds only prose: domain/gst/itc_reversal.py:12 and 90 mention §50 interest as something that runs; services/filing_demo/gstr3b.py:259-277 says plainly "PracticeSync does not compute §50 interest or §47 late fee" and emits Table 5.1 as zeros; domain/gst/gstr3b_computer.py:511-514 hardcodes `intr_ltfee` to zeros. `domain/ai_insight_service.py:23` shows a hardcoded demo string "Estimated late fee ₹500 so far."
findings.ca_experience: For any late GSTR-3B, the return the product prepares carries nil interest and nil late fee, and the CA has to compute §50(1) interest on the net cash liability by hand (18% p.a. from the due date, with the proviso limiting it to the cash-paid portion where the return is filed after the due date but the credit was in the ledger). The Rule 37 report tells the CA credit reverses but not the interest that has accrued on it since it was availed.
findings.market_standard: ClearTax and IRIS compute §50 interest and the §47 late fee (₹50/day, ₹20/day for nil, capped) and show them in Table 5.1 before filing. Tally computes interest on delayed payment.
findings.suggested_fix: Build `domain/gst/interest.py` for §50(1) with its proviso (net cash liability only) and §50(3) for wrongly-availed credit, plus §47 late fee with the nil-return and cap variants, and surface both in Table 5.1 and on the Rule 37 report. The refusal is currently honest but the feature is table stakes.

findings.title: The GSTR-3B screen prints taxable VALUES in the IGST column and shows none of tables 3.1(d), 3.1.1, 3.2, 5 or 5.1
findings.evidence: apps/web/app/gst/gstr3b/page.tsx:308-320 renders the "Zero-rated supplies (Exports / SEZ)" and "Nil-rated / Exempt" rows with `{r(w.outward.zero_rated_paise)}` and `{r(w.outward.nil_exempt_paise)}` placed in the IGST column, with em-dashes under CGST and SGST. Line 321-327 labels the sum of the taxable rows "Total Output Tax". A grep for 'rcm' in the file returns nothing although `working.rcm_inward` is typed at apps/web/lib/data/gst.ts:93-97; there is no 3.1.1 (e-commerce §9(5)), no 3.2 (inter-state to unregistered/composition/UIN, which the backend computes at gstr3b_computer.py:673-687), no Table 5 and no Table 5.1.
findings.ca_experience: The CA reads "Zero-rated supplies ... ₹10,00,000" in a column headed IGST and reasonably concludes ₹10 lakh of IGST is payable on exports. "Total Output Tax" excludes reverse charge. Half the face of the return the product is preparing is simply not on the screen it is prepared on.
findings.market_standard: Every product renders GSTR-3B as the form: 3.1(a)-(e), 3.1.1, 3.2, 4, 5, 5.1 and 6.1, with taxable value and each tax head in their own columns.
findings.suggested_fix: Give Table 3.1 a "Taxable value" column of its own, add the 3.1(d) and 3.1(e) rows, add 3.2 from `inter_sup_*`, and add a Table 5.1 row that states the interest/late-fee position honestly (see GST-21).

findings.title: GSTR-1 has no way to record the real ARN and filing date from the client workspace, so its period lock is never created there
findings.evidence: apps/web/app/clients/[id]/compliance/gst/page.tsx:641-660 offers only "Validate", "CA Approve" and "File (demo)"; there is no action moving a GSTR-1 to `submitted`, and `updateStatus` (line 454-460) never sends `arn` or `filed_date`. GSTR-3B has one on the other screen (apps/web/app/gst/gstr3b/page.tsx:153-162, `markGSTR3BFiled`), GSTR-1 does not. The backend path exists and is the only thing that writes the `filings` row the period lock reads (routers/gst_workspace.py:523-541).
findings.ca_experience: After filing GSTR-1 on the portal, the CA cannot record the ARN against the return in the client GST workspace. The return stays "ca_approved" for ever, the Filing History tab stays empty for GSTR-1, the exception report (which requires status='submitted' with a frozen payload — services/gst_exception_service.py:61-67) can never run, and no §37 period lock is created.
findings.market_standard: Every product records the ARN and filing date per return and uses it to freeze the period.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a "Mark as Filed" action with ARN and filed-date inputs to the GSTR-1 tab, calling the existing PATCH with `status=submitted, ca_approved=true, arn, filed_date`.

findings.title: Table 4(A) rows for import IGST and ISD are permanently zero, and ISD is now compulsory
findings.evidence: apps/api/domain/gst/gstr3b_computer.py:288-305 `itc_avl_rows` emits IMPG, IMPS and ISD as hard zeros with the comment "nothing upstream distinguishes an import or an ISD distribution from any other purchase yet"; all such credit falls into OTH. There is no import-of-goods flag on `purchase_bills` (no `is_import` / bill-of-entry columns in migrations) and no ISD model anywhere (grep for ISD across apps/api finds only this row label).
findings.ca_experience: An importer's Table 4(A)(1) is nil while the portal auto-populates it from ICEGATE via GSTR-2B, so 4(A) will not tie to 2B and the difference has to be explained. A group that distributes common input services across GSTINs has no mechanism at all — and ISD registration became compulsory for common input services from 01-04-2025 (Finance (No.2) Act 2024 amending §2(61) and §20), so this moved from a nicety to a statutory requirement.
findings.market_standard: ClearTax and IRIS both read the IMPG section of GSTR-2B and populate 4(A)(1); IRIS and Cygnet both offer ISD distribution with GSTR-6.
findings.suggested_fix: Add an import flag plus bill-of-entry number/date to purchase bills so IMPG/IMPS can be populated (and matched against 2B's impg section). Treat ISD as a separate roadmap item — it needs its own registration, GSTR-6 and a distribution engine. I could not establish from the repo whether any client is affected today.

findings.title: Composition scheme (CMP-08 / GSTR-4), e-commerce TCS (GSTR-8 and 3B 3.1.1), and GSTR-9C are entirely absent
findings.evidence: A grep for CMP-08, GSTR-4, GSTR-8, GSTR-9C, supeco and 9(5) across apps/api returns only two comments: domain/gst/gstr3b_computer.py:373-382 emits `eco_dtls` as hardcoded zeros with "nothing marks a supply as made through an ECO, and neither side of §9(5) is modelled", and tests/test_gstr1_payload_matches_gstn_utility.py:186-187 records `supeco` as a section this builder does not produce. `clients` has no composition flag.
findings.ca_experience: A composition dealer — a very large share of the SME book a small practice serves — cannot be handled at all: no CMP-08 quarterly statement, no annual GSTR-4, no 1%/5%/6% composition rate computation. A restaurant or seller supplying through Swiggy/Zomato/Amazon has no §9(5) or TCS handling, so their 3.1.1 and Table 14/15 of GSTR-1 are wrong. GSTR-9C (§44(2), turnover above ₹5 crore) does not exist.
findings.market_standard: ClearTax, Zoho Books and TallyPrime all support composition (CMP-08, GSTR-4), and ClearTax/IRIS support GSTR-8 TCS reconciliation and GSTR-9C.
findings.suggested_fix: Sequence by book share: composition first (it is a whole client class the product cannot serve), then §9(5)/TCS marking on sales invoices feeding 3.1.1 and GSTR-1 tables 14/15, then GSTR-9C after GSTR-9 exists.

findings.title: No HSN/SAC master is shipped — every firm builds its own library from nothing
findings.evidence: apps/api/routers/hsn.py:1-16 states the design: "this endpoint used to merge in `public.hsn_master`, a Caflow-shipped global code list. It no longer does — Caflow does not expose a shared HSN/SAC master to users"; `_fetch_library_rows` reads only `firm_hsn_library`. The only ways in are manual add (apps/web/components/lookups/FirmHsnLibraryQuickAddModal.tsx) and a bulk import (apps/web/app/settings/firm-hsn-library/page.tsx:204).
findings.ca_experience: A firm onboarding gets an empty HSN lookup. Every code and rate has to be typed or imported from a spreadsheet the firm sources itself, for every client's product range, before a single invoice can carry a compliant HSN under Rule 46(g). It is the most visible "this product is not finished" moment in onboarding.
findings.market_standard: TallyPrime, Zoho Books and ClearTax all ship the full HSN/SAC master with notified rates and update it with each rate notification; that is the whole reason a user never types an HSN description.
findings.suggested_fix: Ship a seeded HSN/SAC master (chapter, heading, 6-digit and 8-digit, description, notified rate, UQC) as read-only reference merged into search behind the firm's own library, with the firm's entry always winning. The deliberate refusal is defensible for RATES, which move by notification — but the CODES and descriptions do not, and shipping them costs the CA nothing to correct.

findings.title: The 2A/2B reconciliation engine is business logic in TypeScript and parses money with parseFloat × 100
findings.evidence: apps/web/app/gst/reconciliation/page.tsx:210-289 `reconcile(books, gstr2a)` implements the whole matching and match/mismatch classification in the browser, with a 3-paise tolerance invented at line 258. Line 120-128 `toPaise` does `Math.round(parseFloat(s) * 100)` after stripping commas — the exact form CLAUDE.md says was eliminated ("All 61 call sites across 28 files are converted") and which accepts "12abc" as 12 and "1e3" as 1000. `apps/web/lib/money/rupeeInput.ts` is not imported. This is not one of the three parity-pinned exceptions, which are in `gstLine.ts`.
findings.ca_experience: A CSV row with a stray character in an amount silently reconciles at the wrong figure. More broadly, the rule that decides whether an invoice is matched — the thing that determines how much ITC a CA claims — lives in the browser where it is untested, unversioned against the backend, and cannot be reused by the return builder.
findings.market_standard: Not applicable — this is a house-rule violation. But every competitor's matching runs server-side and is persisted.
findings.suggested_fix: Move `reconcile` into `apps/api/domain/gst/` beside a persisted match state (see GST-04), and replace `toPaise` with `lib/money/rupeeInput.ts` for the interim CSV path.

findings.title: Rule 37A has a reason code but no report; Rule 37 has no interest and no posting help
findings.evidence: apps/api/services/itc_register_service.py:36 `RECLAIMABLE_REASONS = ("rule_37", "rule_37a", "section_16_2b", "section_16_2c", "other")` — `rule_37a` is accepted but nothing computes it (grep for 37A across apps/api finds only that tuple and three comments). `services/itc_reversal_service.py:74-152` `rule37_report` lists the bills and the reversal per head but computes no §50 interest, and apps/web/app/gst/gstr3b/page.tsx:533-540 tells the CA the amounts are "Not included in Table 4(B) above" and that they must post the journal by hand — but there is no screen that posts it or that registers it (see GST-13).
findings.ca_experience: Rule 37A (Notification 26/2022, w.e.f. 26-12-2022 — reverse ITC by 30 November where the supplier has not paid the tax by 30 September of the following FY) is never checked, so a client can carry ineligible credit for a year unnoticed. For Rule 37 the CA is shown the amount, told to post a journal manually, and then has to POST an unexposed API endpoint to make it appear in 4(B)(2). The workflow stops one step short of usable.
findings.market_standard: IRIS and ClearTax both run a Rule 37 180-day ageing and a Rule 37A supplier-non-filing check off 2B/2A data and produce the reversal entry.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a "Post this reversal" action from the Rule 37 panel that creates the journal through the posting kernel and registers it in one step, and build the Rule 37A check once supplier GSTR-3B filing status is available from 2B data (GST-04 is a prerequisite).

findings.title: GSTIN check-digit validation is not applied on any GST return path
findings.evidence: apps/api/domain/gst/gstin.py implements the GSTN check-digit algorithm and its docstring (lines 26-33) explains that a transposed PAN "puts the supply into the recipient's GSTR-2B; sent under a GSTIN that is not theirs, the recipient never gets the input tax credit". But `domain/gst/validator.py:14` uses a bare `GSTIN_RE` shape regex, and `core/validators.validate_gstin` (used by routers/gst_workspace.py:373, 566, 962) checks shape plus state code only. `gstr1_from_books` validates no counterparty GSTIN at all. A grep shows `domain/gst/gstin.py` is wired only into the human-entry forms, as CLAUDE.md describes.
findings.ca_experience: A B2B invoice carrying a shape-valid but non-existent customer GSTIN is filed in Table 4A. The customer never sees it in their 2B, chases the CA, and the fix is an amendment in a later return inside the §37(3) window. The check-digit module that would have caught it exists and is not consulted on the filing path.
findings.market_standard: Every product check-digit-validates a GSTIN, and most also validate it live against the GSTN taxpayer-search API before filing.
findings.suggested_fix: Have `GSTValidator.validate_gstin` delegate to `domain/gst/gstin.py`, and run counterparty GSTIN validation as part of the from-books build (GST-16), reporting failures as errors rather than rejecting the whole return.

findings.title: A test encodes the assumption behind the reverse-charge underpayment, so the suite cannot catch it
findings.evidence: apps/api/tests/test_gst_rcm_gstr3b.py:39-45 `test_c4_c5_rcm_net_liability_offsets_itc` — "Classic RCM: ₹18,000 liability and ₹18,000 ITC → net effect zero" — asserts only `r.rcm_igst - r.itc_igst == 0`, never that the RCM tax reaches `net_igst`. No test in the repo asserts anything about `net_*` in the presence of reverse charge. Likewise there is no test for CGST/SGST credit against IGST liability (GST-05), for export-with-payment IGST (GST-02), or for non-GST outward supplies (GST-06).
findings.ca_experience: Indirect: the four highest-value defects in this subsystem all sit in gaps the 130 passing GST tests do not reach, so the suite reads as strong coverage of a computation that is wrong in four places. The tests that exist are careful and well-argued; the missing ones are the load-bearing ones.
findings.market_standard: Not applicable.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a small table of end-to-end 3B scenarios asserting the FILED numbers — RCM-only, export-with-payment, non-GST turnover, intra-state purchase with inter-state sale — rather than asserting the intermediate fields each computation happens to produce.

findings.title: The GST portal integration router is complete, honest and reachable from no screen
findings.evidence: apps/api/routers/gst_portal.py is 165 lines of sync-job and snapshot endpoints; domain/gst/portal_service.py:72-80 carries a correct `TODO(compliance)` explaining the GSP gate and warning that `get_provider` ignores its argument. A grep of apps/web for "gst-portal" returns nothing.
findings.ca_experience: No effect today — nothing is missing that a CA could otherwise do, since the only provider is manual. Worth recording so the seam is not rebuilt when a GSP conversation happens.
findings.market_standard: n/a — this is pre-work for a commercial step CLAUDE.md correctly puts out of scope.
findings.suggested_fix: Leave it. When a GSP is contracted, wire `get_provider`'s switch in the same commit that adds the provider, as the marker says.

findings.title: E-invoicing prepares nothing — no INV-01 JSON, no 30-day reporting-window check, and no e-invoice vs GSTR-1 reconciliation
findings.evidence: apps/api/routers/einvoice.py:8-16 — "These routes RECORD an IRN a human obtained from an IRP; they do not generate one" — and the marker itself notes the 30-day reporting limit for AATO ≥ ₹10 crore from 01-04-2025 is "an IRP VALIDATION". There is no INV-01 payload builder anywhere (grep for INV-01 / SellerDtls / ItemList across apps/api returns nothing), and nothing compares the e-invoiced set against the GSTR-1 B2B table.
findings.ca_experience: For an e-invoicing client the product cannot produce the JSON to upload to the IRP, so the CA keys invoices into the IRP portal by hand — while the same invoices already sit in PracticeSync in full. Nobody is warned when an invoice approaches its 30-day IRN deadline. And because GSTR-1 B2B is auto-populated from e-invoices on the portal, the CA has no way to see where our computed Table 4A differs from what the portal already holds — which is the first thing they check every month.
findings.market_standard: ClearTax, IRIS and TallyPrime generate the INV-01 JSON (Tally and ClearTax push it to the IRP directly), warn on the 30-day window, and reconcile e-invoiced documents against the auto-populated GSTR-1.
findings.suggested_fix: Build the INV-01 payload from `client_sales_invoices` as a prepare-only download (the same posture as the GSTR-1 JSON), add a 30-day ageing warning for AATO ≥ ₹10 crore clients, and add an e-invoice vs GSTR-1 B2B comparison once IRNs are recorded. NIC's sandbox is self-service, so the rails can be tested before any GSP conversation.

maturity.rationale: This is the most carefully reasoned subsystem I have read in a long time and also one that cannot yet be trusted with a filing. The domain layer is genuinely excellent where it has been worked over: the Circular 170/02/2022 Table 4 layout is right and argued from the circular's own words, integer paise discipline is absolute, the GSTR-1 payload has been diffed against the GSTN offline tool key by key (sply_ty, doc_num, CDNUR typ, nil INTR/INTRA), notes inherit their parent invoice's classification under §34, the B2CL threshold is date-aware for Notification 12/2024, and the books-vs-ledger reconciliation shipped with every computation is something no competitor offers. But five defects put a wrong tax number in front of a CA: reverse-charge liability is missing from net payable while its credit is claimed (GST-01); IGST on exports with payment vanishes (GST-02); non-GST supplies vanish (GST-06); CGST/SGST credit is never set off against IGST liability so cash payable is overstated (GST-05); and the reconciliation screen states the repealed 105% Rule 36(4) cap on screen (GST-03). Around those, the two things a CA does most — 2B matching and the annual return — are respectively non-functional (the books are never read; nothing is persisted; nothing writes gstr2a_records) and entirely absent. And a large amount of the best work in the module — amendments, the exception report, the ITC register, advances — has no screen at all, so it does not count yet. The gap between the quality of the reasoning in the code and what a CA can actually do with it is the defining fact about this subsystem.
maturity.would_a_ca_buy_this_module_alone: Not yet — a CA would find the wrong reverse-charge and set-off figures within the first month's 3B, and 2B matching, GSTR-9 and QRMP are the three things they would try first and none of them work.

open_questions_for_owner: What is the actual client mix on the live book — how many are QRMP (turnover ≤ ₹5 cr), how many composition, how many hold more than one GSTIN, and how many have reverse-charge or export activity? Four of the five worst findings (GST-01, GST-05, GST-11, GST-20) rank completely differently depending on that mix, and the CLAUDE.md AA note says the live book is 7 clients, which is too small to answer it.

Is the intended monthly workflow "the books are in PracticeSync, so the return derives from them" or "the books are in Tally, so PracticeSync reconciles and files"? The GST-04 fix looks entirely different in each case: the first needs 2B matched against our own purchase_bills, the second needs a purchase-register import as a first-class object.

Multi-GSTIN (GST-20) is a schema change touching every client-scoped query in the product. Is it in scope now, or is the answer for the next two years "one GSTIN per client record, and a multi-state client becomes two client records"? That decision gates how much of the return engine is worth building on the current shape.

GSTR-9 (GST-10): is the target a full auto-populated annual return with the Table 6 ITC bifurcation and Table 8 2A reconciliation, or the narrower "here is what the year's filed returns add up to, key the rest into the portal"? The two differ by roughly a quarter of engineering time, and the second is deliverable in weeks.

§50 interest and §47 late fee (GST-21) are currently refused honestly. Is that refusal deliberate in the same sense as the state PT/LWF tables — i.e. it stays refused — or is it simply not built yet? Interest under §50(1) with its proviso is computable from data the product already holds, unlike a state minimum wage.

The HSN/SAC master (GST-26) was deliberately removed. Was that about rate accuracy, licensing of the code list, or support burden? If it is rate accuracy, shipping codes and descriptions without rates would remove most of the onboarding pain while keeping the refusal that matters.

Should /gst (the firm-wide tracker, backed by compliance_calendar) and the client GST workspace (backed by gstr1_returns/gstr3b_returns) be reconciled into one filing state, or should the tracker become a read-only view over the returns tables? Today they disagree about whether a return is filed and only one of them creates the period lock (GST-14).

Roughly a third of this subsystem's backend is built, tested and has no screen (GST-13). Is that a deliberate sequencing decision — API first, UI later — or did the UI work simply not get scheduled? It changes whether the next quarter is mostly React or mostly Python.
strengths: The Circular 170/02/2022-GST Table 4 layout is implemented correctly and, unusually, argued from the circular's own test rather than from its list of examples — apps/api/domain/gst/gstr3b_computer.py:66-124 quotes 4(B)(1) and 4(B)(2), explains why "such as" makes the list illustrative, and records that §17(5) belongs in 4(B)(1) and not 4(D). 4(A)/4(B)/4(C) are derived properties (lines 209-260) so they cannot drift from their parts, and 4(C) is what Table 6 spends, never 4(A) — the §49(4) point most implementations get wrong.

The GSTR-1 payload has been diffed field by field against the GSTN Returns Offline Tool rather than written from a spec summary: `sply_ty` vs the `sply_tp` misspelling, the `typ: "OE"` e-commerce indicator, the INTRB2B/INTRAB2B nil codes whose prefixes differ by one letter (gstr1_builder.py:341-358), `doc_num` as the form's fixed position rather than a running count (lines 654-702), and CDNUR's refusal to emit "B2CS" with `_cdnur_unreportable` counting what it drops (lines 483-522). tests/test_gstr1_payload_matches_gstn_utility.py pins each one.

Integer paise discipline is genuinely absolute in the backend, and the two rounding rules are separated by statute rather than by convenience — apps/api/domain/gst/money.py:19-32, 2-decimal rupees for GSTR-1 and whole rupees half-up for GSTR-3B citing §170, with the reasoning that a 2-decimal liability could never be paid from a whole-rupee cash ledger.

Every from-books computation ships with a books-vs-ledger reconciliation (services/gst_return_service.py:807-834) that proves the return's output tax and ITC equal the movement on the GST control accounts — and it survived contact with real data, producing the two hardest fixes in the file: firm-wide control accounts with NULL system_account_key (lines 84-131) and bills cancelled in a later period than they were raised (lines 179-230, the ₹88,141.67 case).

Credit and debit notes inherit their classification from the invoice they adjust under §34 rather than carrying their own columns (services/gst_return_service.py:306-360), which is both the right statutory reading and the shape that cannot drift; and `_note_classification` refuses to guess for an unlinked note.

The staleness gate is a real piece of product thinking: approval is refused when the books have moved since a return was computed, but recording a SUBMITTED filing is not (routers/gst_workspace.py:706-731) — because refusing to let a CA write down what actually happened is the wrong failure. The difference is logged in `stale_at_submission` rather than lost.

The GSTR-3B detail report (services/gst_return_service.py:451-587) reuses the return's own document fetchers and returns its own total so the screen can print both side by side — a detail report that cannot disagree with the summary above it. The B2CL threshold is date-aware for Notification 12/2024 and tests the INVOICE VALUE, not the taxable value (domain/gst/classifier.py:26-54, 121-129).

The filing-demo framework is honest in exactly the way CLAUDE.md demands: services/filing_demo/gstr3b.py:259-277 states in the return itself that §50 interest and §47 late fee are not computed rather than showing a plausible zero, the declaration text is the form's verbatim, signing is shown as happening on the portal, and every reference is a labelled specimen. Two rival demo implementations were deleted rather than left beside it.

The refusals are well-chosen and well-documented where they exist: GSTR-1 Table 11 declines to invent a rate (services/gst_advance_service.py:1-33), the GSP gate carries a scoped TODO(compliance) marker pointing at a real doc section (domain/gst/portal_service.py:72-80), and the ITC register refuses a row that claims more than its journal moved (services/itc_register_service.py:15-25).
subsystem: GST — GSTR-1 builder, GSTR-3B computer, GSTR-9, 2A/2B reconciliation, ITC register and reversals, amendments, correction window, exception reports, advances, filing records and period lock, HSN/SAC, GST portal seam, GST workspace screens and the filing demo
test_coverage_notes: Roughly 40 test modules touch GST; the five core ones I ran (test_gst_engine, test_gstr1_payload_matches_gstn_utility, test_gstr3b_payload_matches_gstn_utility, test_gst_rcm_gstr3b, test_correction_window) give 130 passing in 0.4s. The quality is high and the intent is unusually explicit: tests/test_gstr1_payload_matches_gstn_utility.py:176-190 deliberately PINS the set of sections the builder does not produce (b2ba, b2cla, b2csa, cdnra, cdnura, expa, at, ata, txpd, atadj, atadja, supeco) "so nobody reads this file as 'GSTR-1 is complete'" — that is a model of honest test writing. Domain arithmetic is well covered: Rule 37 proportionate reversal and its rounding-up choice, the Table 4 reversal split, the correction window's "whichever is earlier", the GSTIN check digit against a shared fixture, the whole-rupee §170 rounding, and the frontend/backend GST-line parity vectors in shared/gst-parity-vectors.json. tests/test_gstr3b_screen_contract.py reading the screen's own bindings against a real API response is a genuinely good idea. What is NOT covered is exactly where the defects are, and the pattern is consistent: the tests assert intermediate FIELDS (rcm_igst, itc_book_igst, outward_zero_rated) and almost never the FILED number. Nothing asserts what net_* should be in the presence of reverse charge — tests/test_gst_rcm_gstr3b.py:39-45 instead asserts that liability and credit are equal, which encodes the assumption that produced GST-01. Nothing covers CGST/SGST credit against IGST liability (only the IGST-excess direction, tests/test_gst_engine.py:319-330), export with payment of IGST, non-GST outward supplies, a multi-rate B2C invoice through _build_b2cs, an SEZ or deemed-export invoice reaching the payload, or the HSN digit requirement actually constraining anything. Nothing tests upload_gstr2b against a real GSTR-2B envelope. The frontend has essentially no GST test coverage: apps/web has tests for lib/gst/gstin.ts and lib/gst/rule37Period.ts only, so the /gst Add Filing crash (GST-12), the taxable-value-in-the-IGST-column rendering (GST-22) and the 105% banner (GST-03) all pass CI. Net: the suite proves the parts that were reasoned about carefully and is blind to the joins between them.
what_exists:
Backend. Two domain builders produce the statutory payloads. `domain/gst/gstr1_builder.py` (704 lines) assembles b2b (4A), b2cs (7), b2cl (5), nil (8), cdnr/cdnur (9B), exp (6A), hsn (12) and doc_issue (13) from classified invoices, with `classifier.py` assigning the table category (date-aware B2CL threshold per Notification 12/2024, invoice-value not taxable-value). `domain/gst/gstr3b_computer.py` (747 lines) computes 3.1(a)-(c), 3.2 by place of supply and recipient class, reverse-charge inward tax, the full post-Notification-14/2022 Table 4 (five 4(A) rows, 4(B)(1)/(2), 4(C) as derived properties, 4(D)(1) reclaims), an aggregate Rule 36(4) cap, and a partial §49(5) set-off, then emits GSTN JSON in whole rupees. `money.py` holds the two statutory rounding rules. Supporting domain modules: `itc_reversal.py` (Rule 37 proportionate reversal and the period it belongs in), `correction_window.py` (§37(3)/§39(9)/§16(4)), `amendments.py` + `amendment_proposal.py` (9A/9C/10 nodes and their GSTN grouping), `exception_report.py` (filed payload vs books, document-wise and B2CS-aggregate), `validator.py`, `gstin.py` (check digit), `portal_service.py` (manual-only provider behind a GSP TODO marker).

Services. `gst_return_service.py` (1,256 lines) is the centre: it derives GSTR-1 and GSTR-3B entirely from posted `client_sales_invoices`, `credit_notes`, `sales_debit_notes`, `purchase_bills`, `debit_notes` and `purchase_credit_notes`, resolves notes' classification from their parent invoice under §34, paginates every read by keyset, and returns a books-vs-General-Ledger reconciliation with each result. It also serves a per-line GSTR-3B detail report (3.1a / 4A / 4B1 / 4B2) and a GSTR-9 filing-status summary (not a computation). Alongside: `gst_amendment_service` (walks back over every earlier filed period), `gst_exception_service`, `itc_register_service` (classifies an already-posted journal as a 4(B)(2) reversal or 4(D)(1) reclaim, refusing a row larger than its journal), `itc_reversal_service` (Rule 37 180-day report), `gst_advance_service` (Table 11A/11B), `gst_filing_record_service` (writes the `filings` row the period lock reads), and `filing_demo/` (portal-faithful walk-throughs for GSTR-1, 3B and 9 that transmit nothing).

Endpoints. `/api/gst` (classify, gstr3b/compute, gstr1/build, both from-books, gstr1/with-amendments, gstr3b/detail, two validate routes); `/api/gst-workspace` (1,533 lines: dashboard with QRMP-aware due dates and PMT-06/IFF, save/get/patch-status/delete/recompute for GSTR-1 and 3B, GSTR-9 save/get, GSTR-2B upload, filing history, amendments, exceptions, ITC register, advances, Rule 37); `/api/gst-portal`; `/api/hsn` and `/api/firm-hsn-library`.

Screens. `/gst` (firm-wide filing tracker over `compliance_calendar`), `/gst/gstr1`, `/gst/gstr3b` (compute, approve, mark filed, download JSON, Rule 37 panel), `/gst/reconciliation` (browser-side CSV 2A-vs-purchase-register matcher), and `/clients/[id]/compliance/gst` (1,547 lines: Dashboard, GSTR-1, GSTR-3B with a detail drawer and staleness/recompute, GSTR-9, GSTR-2B Recon, Filing History, plus the shared FilingDemoWizard gated on a server capability probe).

Tables. `gstr1_returns` (also holds GSTR-9 rows via `return_type`), `gstr3b_returns`, `gstr2a_records`, `gstr2b_uploads`, `filings`, `compliance_calendar`, `itc_reversal_register` (migration 285), `firm_hsn_library`.
